newsitem.title: USA: SEC ends probe into Prudential employees - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SEC ends probe into Prudential employees - WSJ.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has dropped its remaining investigations into the possible role former Prudential Securities employees played in selling limited partnerships, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said the SEC sent letters late last week to the former employees, whose actions were under scrutiny.
The SEC had been investigating five former employees who worked at the New York headquarters of the unit's parent company, Prudential Insurance Co of America.
In particular, the regulatory agency was looking into the sale of $8 billion in limited partnerships from 1980 to 1990.
In 1993, Prudential reached a settlement of nearly $2 billion with the SEC. Part of the settlement concerned the allegedly fraudulent sales of limited-partnership interests.
While the settlement ended the SEC's proceedings against Prudential, it had continued to look into the firm's employees involved in the alleged practices.
